title: Andon cord response policy
text: Any operator who detects a defect, a missing part or a safety risk must pull the andon cord immediately. The team leader has the length of the takt time to respond at the station. If the problem cannot be solved within the fixed position, the line stops and the group leader is called. Pulling the andon cord is never penalized; stopping the line to fix a problem is part of jidoka and built-in quality.

title: Standardized work revision process
text: Standardized work sheets are reviewed every time takt time, work sequence or standard in-process stock changes. The team leader drafts the revision, the group leader validates it at the station and the engineering office approves it. The old sheet is removed from the station the same shift and the new version is stored in the central repository with its revision number.

title: Lockout tagout procedure for maintenance
text: Before any maintenance on robots, conveyors or presses, the technician must isolate every energy source, apply a personal lock and tag, and verify zero energy. Each person working on the machine places their own lock. Locks are removed only by their owner after the area is clear. Skipping lockout tagout is a serious safety violation.

title: Supplier quality claim process
text: When a nonconforming part from a supplier is found, quality opens a supplier claim within 24 hours with photos, quantity and lot number. The supplier must send a containment plan in 24 hours and a root cause analysis with an 8D report in ten working days. Claims are closed only after three consecutive clean lots.

title: Kaizen proposal submission policy
text: Every team member can submit kaizen proposals using the one-page A3 format. The proposal describes the current condition, the root cause, the countermeasure and the expected result. The group leader reviews it within one week. Approved kaizen ideas are recognized monthly and the improvement is added to standardized work.

title: Engineering change management procedure
text: Any change to a part, process or tool requires an engineering change request. The request is evaluated by engineering, quality and production for cost, safety and quality impact. After approval, the change point is announced to the line, the first parts are inspected at 100 percent and the documentation is updated before full production.

title: Document control and retention policy
text: Controlled documents such as procedures, work instructions and policies are stored only in the central repository. Each document has an owner, a version number and a review date. Obsolete versions are archived and removed from the shop floor. Quality records are retained for at least ten years.

title: Visitor and contractor safety policy
text: Visitors and contractors must complete the safety induction, wear safety glasses, safety shoes and the assigned vest, and remain with an escort in production areas. Contractors performing maintenance or construction must present a work permit approved by the safety department before starting.

title: Overtime and shift change approval process
text: Overtime must be requested by the group leader at least 48 hours in advance and approved by the area manager and human resources. Shift change requests between team members are registered in the HR system. Weekly overtime may not exceed the limit defined by labor law.

title: Information security and access policy
text: Access to plant systems is granted by role and approved by the area manager. Passwords must be changed every 90 days and cannot be shared. USB drives are blocked on production computers. Confidential engineering drawings may only be sent to suppliers through the approved portal.

title: Ticket INC-1042: MES terminal frozen on assembly line 2
text: The MES terminal at station 14 of assembly line 2 froze and stopped recording vehicle serial numbers. Operators could not confirm torque results. IT restarted the terminal service and the network switch. The terminal recovered after 18 minutes. Root cause: memory leak in the MES client after the last update.

title: Ticket INC-1057: Torque tool not sending data to MES
text: The electric torque tool on the chassis line stopped sending torque results to the MES terminal. Vehicles were held for manual verification. The controller lost its network address after a power outage. IT assigned a fixed address and the tool reconnected. Torque data was recovered from the controller memory.

title: Incident report: Line stop caused by conveyor failure
text: The main conveyor of the paint shop stopped for 42 minutes because of a broken drive chain. The andon was activated and maintenance replaced the chain. 35 bodies were delayed. Countermeasure: add the drive chain to the preventive maintenance plan with monthly inspection and keep a spare chain in stock.

title: Ticket INC-1063: Label printer failure at shipping
text: The label printer at the shipping dock stopped printing barcode labels for finished vehicles. Trucks were delayed 30 minutes. IT replaced the printhead and reinstalled the printer driver. A backup label printer was configured on the same network for future failures.

title: Incident report: Robot welding fault in body shop
text: Welding robot 7 in the body shop generated repeated weld faults and stopped the line. Maintenance found a worn welding tip and a misaligned fixture. The tip was replaced and the fixture recalibrated. Ten bodies were reinspected and two welds were repaired.

title: Ticket INC-1078: User cannot access the document repository
text: A quality engineer could not open procedures in the central document repository after a password change. The account was locked after several failed attempts. IT unlocked the account and reset the password. The user was reminded of the password policy and the self-service reset portal.

title: Incident report: Hybrid battery handling near miss
text: An operator moved a hybrid battery pack without insulated gloves. No injury occurred. The team leader stopped the task and reported the near miss. Root cause: gloves were missing from the station. Countermeasure: add gloves to the station checklist and retrain the team on battery handling.

title: Ticket INC-1085: Network outage in the warehouse
text: Handheld scanners in the parts warehouse lost connection to the network for one hour. Picking for the kanban routes was done on paper. A failed access point was replaced. IT added monitoring alerts for all warehouse access points.

title: Helpdesk FAQ: MES and shop floor systems
text: What should I do if the MES terminal freezes? Pull the andon, inform the team leader and call the IT helpdesk extension 4400. Do not restart the terminal yourself. What if the torque tool does not send data? Hold the vehicle for manual verification and open a ticket. How long does IT take to respond? Line-stop tickets are attended within 10 minutes.

title: Incident report: Paint defect spike on night shift
text: The night shift found a spike of dirt defects in the paint shop. Inspection found a damaged filter in the booth air supply. The filter was replaced, the booth was cleaned and the affected bodies were polished. The filter replacement interval was reduced.

title: Quality report: Door gap nonconformity
text: Final inspection detected door gaps outside specification on 12 vehicles. The 5 Whys analysis traced the problem to a worn locating pin in the door assembly fixture. The pin was replaced and fixture inspection was added to the daily checklist. All affected vehicles were adjusted before shipping.

title: Quality alert: Missing clips on interior trim
text: A customer audit found missing clips on the interior trim panel. Containment: 100 percent inspection of trim panels on the line and in the yard. Root cause: the clip supply bin was empty and the operator continued the cycle. Countermeasure: poka-yoke sensor that detects missing clips.

title: Monthly quality indicators meeting minutes
text: Attendees: quality manager, production managers and supplier quality. Defects per vehicle fell 8 percent this month. Top three defects: paint dirt, door gaps and water leaks. Agreements: launch a kaizen team on water leaks and review the paint booth filter interval.

title: Customer warranty claims analysis
text: Warranty claims for brake noise increased in the last quarter. Analysis of returned parts shows pad material variation from one supplier. Engineering will request a change of pad formula and quality will increase incoming inspection of brake pads.

title: Final inspection audit checklist
text: The final audit checks paint finish, panel gaps, water leaks, electrical functions, torque marks and labels. Five vehicles per shift are audited by the quality audit team. Any critical defect stops shipping of the lot until containment is confirmed.

title: Water leak test procedure
text: Every vehicle passes through the water leak test booth for four minutes. The inspector checks the cabin, trunk and floor with a moisture detector. Leaks are tagged and sent to repair. Repeated leaks in the same area are escalated to the quality engineer.

title: Quality report: Water leak root cause
text: Water leaks on the rear window increased in the leak test booth. The 5 Whys analysis found a sealer bead that was too thin because a sealer nozzle was partially clogged. The nozzle was cleaned and a nozzle check was added to the robot maintenance routine.

title: Andon cord training module for new operators
text: New operators learn when and how to pull the andon cord, what the colors on the andon board mean and how the team leader responds. The module includes a practice session on a training line. Operators must pass a short exam before working on the production line.

title: Onboarding guide for new production team members
text: During the first week new team members complete the safety induction, the Toyota Way introduction, basic skills at the dojo training center and standardized work practice. A trainer accompanies them for their first shifts on the line.

title: Training course: Problem solving with A3 and 5 Whys
text: This course teaches team leaders to define the problem, grasp the current situation at the genba, find the root cause with the 5 Whys and write an A3 report. Participants solve a real quality problem from their area.

title: Safety training: Lockout tagout certification
text: Maintenance technicians are certified in lockout tagout before working on machines. The course covers energy sources, lock and tag rules, zero energy verification and practical exercises. Certification is renewed every year.

title: Training course: MES terminal basics for operators
text: Operators learn to log in to the MES terminal, scan vehicle serial numbers, confirm torque results and report a frozen terminal to the helpdesk. The course explains why manual entries are not allowed.

title: Knowledge transfer from retiring technicians
text: Senior technicians close to retirement record their know-how in video and one-point lessons. Each one mentors a younger technician for six months. The lessons are stored in the central repository and tagged by machine and problem type.

title: Training course: Hybrid battery safe handling
text: Operators who handle hybrid battery packs learn high-voltage risks, the use of insulated gloves and tools, and the emergency response for damaged batteries. The course includes a practical exam.

title: Kanban replenishment procedure
text: When the operator uses the last part of a container, the kanban card is placed in the post. The material handler collects the cards every route and replenishes the parts from the warehouse. Suppliers receive electronic kanban signals to trigger deliveries.

title: Supplier delivery performance report
text: On-time delivery for the month was 96.5 percent. Two suppliers delivered late due to transport problems at the border. Premium freight costs increased. Agreements: review safety stock for imported parts and request recovery plans from late suppliers.

title: Ticket INC-1091: Kanban cards not printing
text: The electronic kanban system stopped printing cards for supplier deliveries. Material handlers used manual cards for one shift. IT found a failed print server and moved the queue to a backup server. Suppliers were informed of the delay in the kanban signals.

title: Procedure for premium freight requests
text: Premium freight is used only to avoid a line stop. The material planner requests it with the reason, the part number and the cost. The logistics manager approves it. Monthly premium freight costs are reviewed with the responsible supplier.

title: Meeting minutes: Supply chain risk review
text: The team reviewed critical parts: semiconductors, wire harnesses and hybrid batteries. Two semiconductor suppliers have long lead times. Agreements: qualify a backup supplier for wire harnesses and increase safety stock of semiconductors to five days.

title: Policy for receiving inspection of purchased parts
text: Receiving inspection verifies quantity, labels and visual condition of every delivery. New parts or suppliers with recent claims receive dimensional inspection. Nonconforming lots are placed on hold in the red area and a supplier quality claim is opened.
